theorems.title: Finite affine maximum gives the unique quadratic optimal plan
assumptions: rho is a Borel probability on R^d, absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure
N is a positive finite integer; y_i are vectors in R^d; c_i are finite real numbers
u(x)=max_i(x dot y_i+c_i); T selects the slope of the smallest maximizing index; lambda=T_pushforward(rho)
theorems.conclusion: T is Borel; T=gradient(u) rho-almost everywhere; (id,T)_pushforward(rho) is the unique minimizer of integral |x-y|^2 over all couplings of rho and lambda. Thus every optimal map equals T rho-almost everywhere.
proof_method: Merge repeated slopes retaining the largest intercept.
Distinct-slope ties lie in finitely many null affine hyperplanes.
The first-index regions are finite intersections of strict and nonstrict affine inequalities.
Use nonnegative slack u(x)-x dot y-c(y); the graph plan attains zero slack.
Quadratic costs differ only through the scalar-product integral when marginals are fixed.
Every optimizer has zero slack and is concentrated on the unique-slope graph.

dual_certificate.psi: |y|^2+2c(y), defined on the finite target support

relaxations: Absolute continuity may be replaced by nullness of the distinct-slope tie hyperplanes.
Convex or bounded source support and quantitative density bounds are unnecessary for this lemma.
dependencies: nonnegative integrable function with zero integral vanishes almost everywhere

theorems.title: Tilted central cells have exactly equal target masses
assumptions: T and S are first-maximizer gradients; mu=T_pushforward(rho); nu=S_pushforward(rho)

conclusion.maps: T and S are the unique quadratic optimal maps from rho to mu and nu respectively.
conclusion.central_cells: A={|x1|<a}; B={|x1|<a+b*x2}, up to rho-null boundaries

theorems.title: Exact Wasserstein distances and unique matching target coupling

conclusion.unique_optimal_target_coupling: Fix -e1 and e1 and send 0 to b e2.

theorems.proof_method: The matching coupling attains a*b^p. Every coupling has cost at least the integral of |y2-z2|^p, equal to a*b^p because every source-target atom y has y2=0. Equality requires identical first coordinates, forcing the matching coupling.
dependencies: Euclidean distance dominates each coordinate difference

theorems.title: Exact L2 difference of the quadratic optimal maps
No uniform W2 exponent above one third
theorems.conclusion: The supremum of ||T_mu-T_nu||_(L2(rho))/W2(mu,nu)^alpha over distinct three-atom probability measures mu,nu in Y is infinity.
theorems.uniformity: d, rho, K, Y, and the exact number of atoms stay fixed; the central atom mass tends to zero.

theorems.title: No uniform W1 exponent above one quarter
theorems.conclusion: The supremum of ||T_mu-T_nu||_(L2(rho))/W1(mu,nu)^alpha over distinct three-atom probability measures mu,nu in Y is infinity.

theorems.title: Necessary exponent ceiling for Wp to L2 stability
assumptions: same fixed cube and uniform source as 374.W2_exponent_obstruction
theorems.conclusion: No target-uniform bound ||T_mu-T_nu||_L2 <= C*Wp(mu,nu)^alpha holds, even with exactly three atoms.
theorems.witness_ratio: 2^(alpha-1)*sqrt(1+a^2)*a^(1/2-alpha*(1+1/p)), for b=a/2 and a down to 0
theorems.caution: This does not establish a sharp global upper bound for general p.

theorems.title: Exact finite Lq distance and further necessary exponent ceilings

conclusion.obstruction: For 1<=p<infinity, no uniform Lq-map estimate in Wp^alpha can hold when alpha>p/(q*(p+1)).

theorems.caution: No positive global upper estimate for general p,q is proved.

theorems.title: Failure of uniform map continuity in essential supremum norm
assumptions: b=a/2 and a tends down to zero

conclusion.target_distances: Wp tends to zero for every 1<=p<=infinity

theorems.title: Exact W2 identity for finite atomic targets on the line
assumptions: rho is uniform probability on [-1,1] in R
mu and nu are finite atomic probability measures on R
T_mu and T_nu denote the unique quadratic optimal maps from rho
proof_method: Construct increasing quantile step maps using consecutive source intervals of the atom masses.
Their integrated potentials are finite convex piecewise-affine maxima, so the finite-affine lemma proves map optimality and uniqueness.
Use the nonnegative layer-cake identity after shifting both bounded target variables by a common M.
For any coupling, P(U>s,V>t)<=min(P(U>s),P(V>t)); pairing two quantiles of one uniform variable attains equality at every threshold.
This pairing maximizes the scalar product and minimizes quadratic cost.

assumptions_audit.source_absolute_continuity: Used for null affine tie sets and hence uniqueness in the finite-affine lemma.
assumptions_audit.finite_second_moments: Source assumption plus bounded finite target support make all quadratic costs finite.
assumptions_audit.distinct_slopes: Distinct in the explicit family; the general lemma merges repeats.
assumptions_audit.parameter_geometry: 0<b<a and a+b<1 prevents sign changes and clipping of central widths.
assumptions_audit.dimension: Transverse coordinate requires d>=2; dimension-one finite atomic targets instead satisfy an exact Lipschitz identity.
assumptions_audit.atom_masses: Exactly three positive atoms for each a, but no uniform positive lower bound on the central mass a.
assumptions_audit.atom_separation: Distinct atoms within each target remain at least distance 1 apart.
assumptions_audit.source_fixed: K=Y=[-1,1]^d and rho uniform are unchanged with a.
assumptions_audit.map_vs_target_coupling: Unique source-to-target optimality does not make the common-source target-to-target coupling optimal.

nonclaims: No global W2^(1/3) upper stability bound is proved.
